```{r setup}
library(pkexport)
```
This vignette shows how to go from raw clinical PK tables to a file ready for Monolix, using the example data included in the package.

## Cleaning raw data with standardize_pk_data()

Clinical PK data usually arrive as three separate tables: doses, drug levels, and patient covariates. The package includes a small made-up example of each, for 4 patients on IV cefepime. Times are hours since midnight on each patient's first dosing day.

```{r}
head(pk_doses)
head(pk_levels)
pk_covariates
```

`standardize_pk_data()` stacks doses and levels into one table sorted by patient and time, then adds two columns:

- `TIME`: hours since that patient's first dose
- `TAD`: hours since the most recent dose (level rows only)

```{r}
std <- standardize_pk_data(pk_doses, pk_levels, pk_covariates)
head(std, 8)
```

Two patients show why TAD matters. Patient P03's third dose was given 1.5 hours late, so the trough's TAD is 6.25 hours instead of the scheduled 7.75. Patient P04 has a level labeled "trough" that was actually drawn 0.75 hours after a dose.

```{r}
std[std$EVENT == "level", c("ID", "TIME", "TAD")]
```
